title: The bath and the tide

data.source: Two-process model equations (Daan, Beersma and Borbely 1984) with and without the body-clock term, compared with the published summary of Akerstedt and Gillberg 1981. No raw data.
data.licence: published summary statistics, cited; no data copied

prediction: A count-to-threshold loop with no outside clock gives longer sleep after every longer time awake, and a day of 22.5 hours; the published finding is that sleep begun at 07:00 or 11:00, after 24 to 28 hours awake, is the shortest.
baseline: The two-process model of sleep: the same loop with thresholds that follow a 24 hour body clock.
why: As predicted, the plain count-and-cut loop says more time awake always means more sleep, which is not what was found. It works only after a clock-driven threshold is added, and that addition is the two-process model.
